title: A Lindbladian for holographic Brownian motion
abstract: We derive a Lindbladian description of holographic Brownian motion in the high-temperature regime. Starting from the influence functional for a trailing string endpoint, we identify the corresponding quantum master equation and prove that it is completely positive and trace-preserving. We determine the coefficients of the Lindbladian explicitly for two holographic backgrounds: the BTZ black hole and the AdS$_5$ black brane, restricting in the latter case to the endpoint fluctuation along the $x^1$-direction. We then analyze the time evolution of phase-space moments, energy relaxation, and steady states.
summary: This paper develops a rigorous Lindblad master equation describing holographic Brownian motion, which models heavy particle diffusion in a hot plasma using the AdS/CFT correspondence. By expanding the string endpoint influence functional and taking the Markovian limit, the authors derive dissipation coefficients for specific black hole backgrounds. The results confirm that the system thermalizes correctly, satisfying equipartition laws.
main_problem: The paper derives a Lindbladian description for holographic Brownian motion, modeling the stochastic dynamics of a heavy probe quark coupled to a thermal plasma.
main_result: It successfully constructs a completely positive and trace-preserving quantum master equation describing the system's time evolution in the Markovian limit. The analysis confirms energy relaxation approaches classical equipartition values under appropriate conditions.
method: The methodology involves deriving an influence functional from the Nambu–Goto action, applying the Schwinger–Keldysh formalism, and taking a high-temperature local Markovian expansion to yield the Lindblad generator.
model_or_system: The system is holographic Brownian motion, modeled by an open string endpoint fluctuation in AdS space coupled to a thermal bath. The dynamics are captured by a master equation involving dissipation coefficients derived from Green's functions for specific backgrounds like BTZ and AdS$_5$.

why_interesting: This work provides a concrete realization of open quantum system dynamics (Lindbladian evolution) derived from fundamental gravitational/string theory principles (AdS/CFT), offering tools to study thermalization in strongly coupled systems relevant to condensed matter physics.
